items.note: This follows the spec's dashboard recipe closely. It opens on a white header with a greeting and a crescent-and-sparkle glyph, then a row of four saturated stat tiles carrying icons in cream plates and big bold numbers, a cream chart panel with flat yellow bars, and ink pills on ledges. The tiles read like the reference's color stat tiles. The full-height blue activity panel next to them adds a second large saturated field, though, and pulls the eye away from the tiles.

The tiles stack two by two and keep their hues and plates. Above them, though, come two rows of chunky nav, search and avatar pills, then a large glyph that pushes the title into a narrow right column, so the title wraps. This is much heavier than the reference's compact phone header (dot, one pill, menu) with centered text below.

The night version is faithful to the reference's night screen. It has a navy page, an indigo sidebar and panels, white pills with ink labels, and the stat tiles at full strength. The type and hierarchy match the light screen. The reference's navy band with white type carries over well.

The palette is right: navy page, indigo nav pills and a white selected pill. It has the same stacked pill rows and squeezed title next to the glyph as the light phone screen, so the first screen is mostly chrome before any data, unlike the reference's lean phone header.

This is a strong page-header band. It is a full-width blue band in the area's hue that sags at the bottom, with a bold white title and a sparkle, cloud and shaded sun disc in its trailing third. Below sit filter pills with the white dot and a calm table with tags and dot status pills. The silhouette is clearly the reference's yellow topic hero. The shape cluster is thin and generic next to the reference's composed blob-photo vignette.

The band keeps its hue and its sag on the phone, with the title, the lead and one shaded disc. The filter pills wrap with the selected ink pill and dot. The full-width search input and table frame are well spaced. This is close to the reference's stacked yellow phone hero.

The blue band holds against the navy page with a clean arc, the filter pills turn indigo with a white selected pill, and the table sits on an indigo frame with quiet rules. It is consistent with the reference's night palette.
This is the dark version of the phone projects screen. The band, pills and input are all on indigo, the hierarchy and arc are kept, and contrast is good throughout.

It has a header band with a breadcrumb, a bold title, a white status tag and a two-color disc. Below are tab pills with the ink selected state and a cream panel holding a yellow cover with a crescent-shaded disc, a sparkle and a row of bold facts. The cover follows the system's rule for items without images. The page ends abruptly, with a lot of empty white below one panel.

The band and tabs carry over well. The yellow cover, though, sits off-center inside the cream panel with an empty strip on its right. It also stacks right under the blue band, so the phone shows two large saturated fields at once, and the description is pushed below the fold. That is more crowded than the reference's one field per screen.

The night version keeps the blue band, an indigo panel and a yellow cover. The white selected tab and the bold facts read clearly. It is consistent with the light detail page and with the reference's night look.
It has the same structure as the light phone detail page, on navy and indigo. The off-center cover and the two stacked large fields again crowd the first screen ahead of the content.

This is a green header band in the team area's hue with a sag arc, a sparkle, a cloud and a pink shaded disc, above a clean table. In the table, initials avatars sit on crescent-shaded hue discs, the header row is cream and the rows have 1px rules. It is consistent with the category-hue system. Like the other bands, the shapes use the same layout as on the projects page.

The green band stacks with its arc and a disc. The table scrolls inside its frame, as the spec intends, and the bold names and crescent avatars are readable at phone size. It is a faithful compact version.
The green band sits on navy, the table frame is indigo, and the avatar discs keep their hues. It is clean and consistent with the reference's night appearance.
This is the dark version of the phone team screen. The band, the arc and the table on indigo are intact, and the avatars and link text read well against navy.

findings.summary: Every header band reuses the same sparkle, cloud and disc in the same spots, and on phones only a lone disc is left. The reference composes each hero's shapes as a deliberate vignette (blob photo, offset edge, cloud, sparkles), so these bands read as stamped rather than designed.

The phone app shell stacks a row of nav pills plus a row with the search field, a search pill and an avatar above every page, so the first screen is mostly controls. On the overview, a large glyph also squeezes the title into a narrow column. The reference's phone header is one compact row (mark, one pill, menu) with the title centered below.

On phones, the detail page's yellow cover stacks right under the blue header band, so two large saturated fields fill one screen. The cover also sits off-center in its cream panel and pushes the description below the fold. The reference keeps one field per screen and centers its compositions.

The dashboard sets a full-height blue activity panel beside the row of saturated stat tiles, so two strong field areas compete. The spec makes the tile row the screen's one field, and the reference sets its color tiles against white with nothing saturated next to them.
